title: PRIME MINISTER OF NEPAL CALLS ON THE PRESIDENT OF INDIA
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 6:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Prime Minister of Nepal, Rt. Hon’ble Mr. Balendra Shah, called on the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan today (November 23, 2026).
Welcoming Prime Minister Shah to Rashtrapati Bhavan, the President congratulated him on the strong mandate for his government in the March 2026 elections, and wished him success in his efforts to fulfill the aspirations of the people.
The President expressed her condolences for the loss of life caused by the Bhotekoshi floods. She said that as always, in this difficult time, India has stood by Nepal, providing prompt humanitarian assistance and technical support, and will continue to do so as a close partner in the recovery and reconstruction efforts.
The President underlined that climate change is a shared challenge for both our nations, and we must work together to strengthen early warning systems and disaster management.
The President said that the unique and multi-faceted India-Nepal relations are based on our shared civilizational heritage and the deep cherished bonds between the people of the two countries.
She said that the Joint Vision document announced during this visit reflects the aspirations of the people of both our nations, especially the youth. She expressed confidence that it will provide a clear direction for our future cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, development partnership, connectivity, cultural and people to people exchanges, as well as in new and emerging sectors such as start-ups, digital services, space and innovation.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi joins the Shabad Kirtan on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
subtitle:
The entire Sikh tradition is synonymous with the spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture: PM

Today, conflicts are underway in numerous parts of the world, with countless innocent people and families facing violence and unrest; In such times, to ensure peace in every corner of the globe, safety for every family, and the opportunity for every individual to live with dignity, the spirit of 'Sarbat Da Bhala' becomes all the more vital: PM

Every youth of the nation should be free from addiction, fulfill their dreams, study well, and bring pride to their family and nation; Families play a major role in this effort, and together, our Sangat, Gurudwaras, and social organisations can guide the youth and give them the courage to choose the right path: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today joined the Shabad Kirtan on the sacred occasion of the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Addressing the gathering on the occasion, the Prime Minister opened his remarks with the greeting Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh! Bowing with reverence to Guru Nanak Dev Ji in the sacred atmosphere and expressing heartfelt gratitude for the opportunity to participate in the Shabad Kirtan, he extended festive greetings to the nation.“I extend countless greetings to all countrymen on the occasion of Parkash Purab,” remarked Shri Modi.
Describing every Shabad of Gurbani and every melody of Kirtan as far more than mere music, the Prime Minister characterized it as a spiritual practice in itself and like diving into an ocean of knowledge. “Therefore, whenever I receive an invitation for such an event, whenever I get the opportunity, I definitely attend the Sangat and Kirtan,” remarked PM Modi.
Recalling Guru Nanak Dev Ji's teaching of Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo as a natural part of his life from childhood, the Prime Minister spoke fondly of bowing in Gurdwaras, immersing in Gurbani, experiencing the joy of Seva, partaking in Langar, and paying obeisance at Sri Harmandir Sahib on numerous occasions. “Old colleagues would know that I have also spent a lot of time in Punjab, and that period has been one of the most special memories of my life,” remarked Shri Modi.
Expressing gratitude for continually receiving the company of Sikh saints by the Guru's grace, including the privilege of hosting numerous saints and scholars at the Prime Minister's residence, Shri Modi noted the distinct spiritual energy felt through their presence at the event and felicitated all Sikh brothers. “On this occasion, I bow to all saints and scholars,” remarked PM Modi.
Highlighting that this year's Parkash Purab coincides with the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, who laid down his life on the very soil of Delhi to protect the nation's identity, faith, belief, and values, the Prime Minister noted that even after 350 years, the inspiration of that sacrifice remains deeply ingrained in the soil and every corner of the nation. “Every citizen of the country will always remain grateful to him for it,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Observing that the entire Sikh tradition has been synonymous with sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture, exemplified by the martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji as well as the unabated spirit during the freedom struggle, the Prime Minister paid tribute to Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji for his vital role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement and lifelong dedication to service. “This year also marks the completion of one hundred years of his martyrdom; on this occasion, I bow to him as well,” noted PM Modi.
Recalling that India endured centuries of slavery and that even during its most difficult historical periods the Gurus kept alive the flame of protecting the nation, the Prime Minister emphasized that today's great national resolves and the goal of Viksit Bharat can only be achieved through their inspiration and ideals. “Therefore, it is the responsibility of all of us to keep Sikh traditions and the heritage of Sikhi ahead as a beacon of light,” asserted Shri Modi.
Detailing how the government has fulfilled this responsibility with complete faith over the past 12 years, the Prime Minister cited the celebrations of the 350th Parkash Purab of Guru Gobind Singh Ji and the 550th Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji across India and abroad. He noted that commemorative coins and postage stamps were released, special trains were run, Gurbani programs were organized nationwide, and a national event was held at the Red Fort to mark the 400th Parkash Purab of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. “With this same spirit, we are currently also observing the 350th Martyrdom Day of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji,” noted PM Modi.
Noting that the nation will observe the next Veer Bal Diwas on December 26, the Prime Minister explained that the national observance was initiated to pass on the immortal saga of the brave Sahibzadas' martyrdom and Mata Gujri's resolve to the younger generation. “When our children learn about the circumstances of that era, how the Sahibzadas and Gurus attained martyrdom, and how our faith remained protected, this knowledge and inspiration will build youth dedicated to the nation,” asserted Shri Modi.
Pointing out that efforts to celebrate the glory of the Gurus extend beyond India's borders, the Prime Minister recalled his recent visit to Khalsa Diwan, the oldest Gurdwara in the Philippines, where the Government of India is supporting its redevelopment. “It is our effort that the light of our Gurus reaches every person, and with their blessings, India touches new heights,” affirmed PM Modi.
Quoting the Ardas prayer ‘Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhane Sarbat Da Bhala’, the Prime Minister noted that Gurbani imparts the universal teaching of working for the welfare of all. “The thought of wishing well for everyone awakens in the mind only when we begin to consider everyone as our own,” observed Shri Modi.
Referring to ongoing conflicts around the world where innocent people and families face violence and unrest, the Prime Minister emphasized the universal need for peace, safety for every family, and a life of dignity for every individual. “In such times, the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala becomes even more important,” asserted PM Modi.
Observing that the greatest test of the life values imparted by Guru Sahib takes place in everyday life, the Prime Minister drew attention to the pressing societal challenge of drugs. “When a young person falls into the grip of addiction, the dreams of the entire family shatter along with them,” observed Shri Modi.
Calling for every youth in India to be free from addiction so they can study well, fulfill their dreams, and bring pride to their families and the nation, the Prime Minister underscored the vital role of families, the Sangat, Gurdwaras, and social institutions in guiding youth toward the right path, before concluding with Parkash Purab greetings and the traditional Sikh salutations. “I am confident that with Guru Sahib's grace and the collective efforts of society, we will be able to give our new generation a safe and bright future,” affirmed PM Modi.

content:
Guru Pyari Saadh Sangat Ji, Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!
Revered saints of the Sikh community, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji, Chief Minister of Delhi Sister Rekha Gupta ji, my colleagues in Parliament, other ministers of the Delhi Government, all distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen,
In this sacred atmosphere, I respectfully bow to Guru Nanak Dev Ji. I extend lakh-lakh greetings to all the people of the country on the occasion of Prakash Parv. On this holy occasion of Guru Purab, I sincerely thank Taranjit Singh Sandhu ji for giving me the opportunity to participate in this Shabad Kirtan.
Friends,
Every word of Gurbani and every note of Kirtan is not merely music. It is a form of spiritual practice in itself. It is like diving into an ocean of knowledge. Therefore, whenever I receive an invitation to such an event, whenever I get an opportunity, I make it a point to be present in the Sangat and Kirtan.
Friends,
Guru Nanak Dev Ji used to say: Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo. These teachings have been a natural part of my life. Bowing my head at Gurdwaras, immersing myself in Gurbani and experiencing spiritual bliss, finding joy in service, and then partaking in Langar, this has been a continuous part of my journey from childhood to my days as an organisational worker. Many times, I have had the good fortune of bowing my head at Sri Harmandir Sahib. Old colleagues know that I spent a considerable amount of time in Punjab as well, and that period remains one of the most special memories of my life.
Brothers and sisters,
By Guru’s grace, I have continued to receive the company of Sikh saints. At the Prime Minister’s residence too, I have had the privilege of hosting many Sikh saints and Gyanis. Even today, the presence of our saints at this gathering is creating a unique spiritual energy. On this occasion, I bow to all the saints and Gyanis. I extend my greetings to all Sikh brothers and sisters.
Friends,
This year’s Prakash Parv is accompanied by another sacred remembrance. This year marks 350 years since the martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. It was here on the soil of Delhi that Guru Sahib sacrificed his life for the protection of the identity of this nation, for faith, belief, and values. Three hundred and fifty years have passed since that event, yet the inspiration of that sacrifice remains deeply embedded in the soil of India and in every particle of this nation. The people of this country will always remain grateful to him.
Friends,
The spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture has always been synonymous with the Sikh tradition. The martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji reminds us of this. This spirit continued uninterrupted even during the struggle for Independence. As our Lieutenant Governor explained in detail, Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji himself is a shining example of this tradition. He played an important role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement. He dedicated his entire life to service. This year also marks one hundred years since his martyrdom. On this occasion, I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.
Friends,
India endured centuries of slavery. During the most difficult periods in our history, our Gurus kept the flame of protecting the nation burning. Today, when great national resolutions stand before us, when the goal of a Developed India lies ahead of us, this journey can be completed only through the inspiration of our Gurus and the strength of their ideals. Therefore, it is our responsibility to keep Sikh traditions and the heritage of Sikhi shining before society like a beacon of light.
Friends,
Over the past twelve years, we have sincerely tried to fulfil this responsibility. We celebrated the 350th Prakash Parv of Guru Gobind Singh Ji. We celebrated the 550th Prakash Parv of Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Numerous ceremonies were organised across India and abroad. Commemorative coins and postage stamps were issued. Special trains were operated. Programmes dedicated to Gurbani were organised throughout the country. Similarly, on the 400th Prakash Parv of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, a national event was held at the Red Fort. With the same spirit, we are currently commemorating the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.
Friends,
One month from now, on 26 December, the country will observe another Veer Baal Diwas. We began observing this day nationally because it is our responsibility to take to the younger generation the immortal saga of the martyrdom of the Sahibzadas, the resolve of Mata Gujri, and that unparalleled courage and valour. When our children learn about the circumstances of those times, when they understand how the Sahibzadas and the Gurus made the supreme sacrifice and how our faith was protected through their sacrifices, that knowledge and inspiration will create youth dedicated to the nation.
Our efforts to honour the Gurus are not limited to India. Just a few days ago, I was in the Philippines. There too, I visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara, the oldest Gurdwara in the Philippines. The Government of India is also supporting the redevelopment of the Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara. Our effort is that the light of our Gurus should reach every person. With their blessings, India should continue to reach new heights.
Friends,
In our Ardas, we say: Nanak Naam Chardi Kala, Tere Bhaane Sarbat Da Bhala. This teaching of wishing well for all comes to us from Gurbani. And the thought of working for everyone's welfare arises only when we begin to regard everyone as our own.
Friends,
Today, conflicts are taking place in many parts of the world. Many innocent people and families are facing violence and unrest. In such times, the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala, Sarbat Da Bhala, becomes even more important, so that there may be peace everywhere, every family may remain safe, and every individual may have the opportunity to live with dignity.
Friends,
The greatest test of the values given to us by Guru Sahib comes in our everyday lives. Today, one such challenge before our society is the problem of drugs. Because when a young person falls into the grip of addiction, the dreams of an entire family are shattered along with him.
Friends,
Every young person in the country should be free from addiction. They should fulfil their dreams, study well, progress in life, and bring honour to their family and the nation. In this effort, the role of families is extremely important. Our Sangat, our Gurdwaras, and our social institutions can together guide young people and give them the courage to choose the right path. I am confident that with Guru Sahib’s blessings and the collective efforts of society, we will be able to provide a safe and bright future for our younger generation. With this sentiment, I once again extend lakh-lakh greetings to all of you on the sacred Prakash Parv of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj.
Waheguru Ji Ka Khalsa, Waheguru Ji Ki Fateh!

Thank you very much!

title: Joint Press Release on the State Visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal to India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
At the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, H.E. Mr. Balendra Shah, Prime Minister of Nepal, undertook a State Visit to India from 22-23 November 2026. He was accompanied by a high-level official delegation. This visit was Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s first visit to India after his assumption of office.
Prime Minister Shah was accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan. He paid homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat. Prime Minister Shah called on Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu. External Affairs Minister, Dr. S. Jaishankar also called on Prime Minister Shah.
Prime Minister Modi held talks with Prime Minister Shah and hosted a luncheon in his honour. The discussions between the two leaders covered key areas of bilateral cooperation and regional issues of mutual interest as well as global developments.
Prime Minister Shah acknowledged with appreciation India’s humanitarian and technical support and solidarity in the aftermath of the devastating Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi floods that caused significant loss of life and destruction of property in Nepal.
Prime Minister Modi reaffirmed India’s unwavering support to Nepal’s development journey as a close friend and neighbour. India will extend development assistance of INR 15,000 crores (NPR 24,000 crores) comprising a grant assistance of INR 3,500 crores (NPR 5,600 crores) for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects in Nepal; and a Rupee-denominated Line of Credit of INR 11,500 crores (NPR 18,400 crores) for energy sector projects. Specific projects as well as modalities for the provision of development assistance will be finalized through mutual consultations.
Both leaders noted with satisfaction the ongoing progress in the implementation of development projects in Nepal, including the High Impact Community Development Projects (HICDP). They noted the progress achieved in the construction of the National Police Academy in Nepal, being built with assistance from Government of India. Both leaders also welcomed the announcement of setting up an Agro-Industrial Park in Chitwan with grant assistance from India.
The two leaders adopted a Joint Vision for a “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal”. The Joint Vision statement provides the roadmap for an aspirational and future-oriented partnership between India and Nepal. It encompasses initiatives to augment traditionally strong areas of bilateral cooperation such as economic and development partnership, connectivity, energy and water resources, and people-to-people linkages, as well as new synergies in the domains of climate resilience, disaster mitigation and management, sports, start-ups, digital services, space and innovation.
The leaders noted the on-going discussions on civil aviation matters, aimed at enhancing connectivity and boosting bilateral economic engagement. Both sides agreed that the existing unidirectional B345 Kathmandu-Bhairahawa-Lucknow route, will be made bidirectional. Technical consultations will be held to finalize the modalities in this regard and to address other civil aviation proposals from both sides currently under discussion.
Prime Minister Modi announced a new connectivity avenue for Nepal’s transit trade through Deendayal Port (Kandla, Gujarat). Further, access to Paradip port (Odisha) will also be made available once requisite infrastructure is in place.
The two leaders underlined the importance of improving cross-border connectivity and enhancing border infrastructure, through the establishment of new railway lines, bridges, Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and petroleum pipelines.
The two Prime Ministers flagged off the inaugural Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur. This rail service will not only improve connectivity but also give a fillip to religious and cultural tourism along the Ramayana Circuit, and strengthen the civilisational ties between India and Nepal. The leaders agreed to explore similar connections to develop Buddhist and Shiv-Shakti religious tourism circuits.
The two leaders announced the finalization of the Field Location Survey for the proposed Raxaul–Kathmandu electrified broad-gauge railway line, and announced that the two sides will collaborate in the development of the East-West Railway in Nepal.
The two leaders laid virtually the foundation stone for a new ICP at Banbasa and welcomed the progress in the construction of the ICPs at Bhairahawa, Sunauli and Dodhara-Chandani. Three ICPs between India and Nepal are already operational.
A new cross-border motorable bridge between Dharchula (India) and Darchula (Nepal) was inaugurated by the leaders. This will help improve direct connectivity between Western Nepal and India.
The leaders noted with satisfaction the progress in joint field work relating to maintenance and repair of boundary pillars, and directed the Foreign Secretaries to work on the outstanding boundary issues.
In an expansion of cross-border petroleum infrastructure between India and Nepal, the leaders dedicated to the people of Nepal phase II of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj Pipeline. The two leaders also laid virtually the foundation stone for the development of a petroleum terminal at Jhapa, Nepal and emphasized the importance of early commencement of work on the petroleum pipeline between Siliguri and Jhapa. Both sides agreed to explore cooperation in the construction of gas pipelines between India and Nepal.
Both sides expressed satisfaction at the bilateral progress in the hydropower sector, in keeping with the India-Nepal Joint Vision Document for Power Sector Cooperation and the Long Term Power Trade Agreement. Both sides welcomed the active engagement of Indian companies in the hydro-power sector in Nepal, and agreed to ensure the expeditious completion of various hydropower projects being developed by Indian companies in Nepal. On this occasion, the two leaders laid virtually the foundation stone for the 669 MW Lower Arun Hydro-Electric Project.
The two leaders directed the Pancheshwar Development Authority and the Joint Committee on Water Resources to finalise the Detailed Project Report of the Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project expeditiously and commence work on the implementation of the project. Both leaders also agreed on the need to accelerate work on the DPR of the Saptakoshi and Sunkoshi multipurpose projects to harness water resources for mutual benefit and mitigate the impact of floods.
The two sides noted with satisfaction the progress regarding the formation of JVs for two high-capacity cross-border transmission lines between Inaruwa (Nepal) - New Purnea (India) and Dododhara (Nepal) – Bareilly (India).
In an expansion of India’s development and capacity-building support to Nepal, the two leaders agreed that India would set up an off-shore IIT campus in Nepal. This will serve as a force-multiplier in Nepal’s education sector and also promote job creation. Both leaders welcomed the expanding co-operation between India and Nepal in the area of technology, including start-ups and digital and financial connectivity.
Both sides acknowledged the need to mutually facilitate smoother access to services, including banking and telecom, for the people of one country residing in the other.
The following Memoranda of Understanding were exchanged between the two sides during the visit:
i. Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for Academic and Research Collaboration between National Forensic Sciences University, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, and Crime Investigation Department, Nepal Police.
ii. MoU between Rashtriya Raksha University (RRU), India, and National Police Academy (NPA), Nepal.
iii. MoU between National Centre for Good Governance, Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances, Government of India, and Nepal Administrative Staff College, Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, Government of Nepal, on Capacity Building Training Programme for Civil Servants of Nepal.
iv. MoU between Government of India and Government of Nepal on Cooperation in the field of Ayurveda and other Traditional Systems of Medicine.
v. MoU between Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), Government of India, and Ministry of Information and Communication (MOIC), Government of Nepal, on Establishment of Satellite Communication (SATCOM) Network for the Utilization of South Asia Satellite.

title: Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal: Re-imagining the Partnership
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 4:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
At the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Shri Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of Nepal, H.E. Balendra Shah, paid a State Visit to India from 22 to 23 November 2026. The two Prime Ministers held cordial, substantial and forward-looking talks in New Delhi and undertook a comprehensive review of the bilateral relationship.
The two leaders acknowledged that the age-old, civilisational ties between India and Nepal have developed into a multifaceted partnership that derives strength from deep people-to-people linkages apart from adherence to the principles of mutual respect and benefit.
Nepal conveyed its appreciation for India's prompt humanitarian and search-and-rescue assistance following the floods and debris flows in the Rasuwa–Trishuli basin and elsewhere in August 2026. The leaders agreed to remain engaged on the further support to be provided for Nepal’s reconstruction efforts.
The two leaders agreed that the bilateral partnership should reflect contemporary political, economic and technological realities, and should be based on an updated and forward-looking legal framework, where existing bilateral agreements,including the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship, could be reviewed on the basis of mutual consent. All outstanding matters, including those related to water resources, energy, trade & commerce and boundary, are to be resolved through mutual discussion and dialogue.
To translate the India-Nepal relationship into a modern and results-oriented partnership that delivers tangible benefits to the people of both countries, the two leaders have adopted this ‘Joint Vision’ that focuses on the aspirations of the people of India and Nepal, especially the youth; and will provide a roadmap for the future of the bilateral partnership with a focus on the following ten pillars:
I. Comprehensive Economic and Development Partnership
India's national vision of ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’ and Nepal’s national aspiration of ‘Samunnat Nepal’ have several complementarities that could be leveraged to further enhance the extensive economic ties between the two countries. This would include:
i. Reviewing the enabling frameworks/agreements for trade and investment between both countries to facilitate a more comprehensive economic partnership.
ii. To open new transit connectivity and air routes to enable improved access and strengthen connectivity.
iii. Cooperation for the establishment of cross-border special economic zones/parks for export-oriented manufacturing near the India-Nepal border so as to create linkages with supply chains in manufacturing and other processing industries, and co-operate in the development of IT parks.
iv. Indian investments will be encouraged in Nepal's priority sectors, including through the conclusion of arrangements that enhance investor-confidence and the ease of doing business.
v. India will extend development assistance of INR 15,000 crores (NPR 24,000 crores) comprising a grant assistance of INR 3,500 crores (NPR 5,600 crores) for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects in Nepal; and a Rupee-denominated Line of Credit of INR 11,500 crores (NPR 18,400 crores) for energy sector projects. Specific projects as well as modalities for the provision of development assistance will be finalized through mutual consultations.
II. Physical and Digital Connectivity:
Connectivity is a key enabler for deepening of economic cooperation and strengthening people-to-people ties. Recognizing the significant progress made in this area, both leaders welcomed the launch of direct express rail service between Ayodhya (India) and Janakpur (Nepal) and motorable bridge across Mahakali River between Dharchula (India) and Darchula (Nepal). They further agreed to:
i. Expedite the ongoing construction of the ICPs at Bhairahawa (Nepal) and Sunauli (India), and new ICPs at Banbasa (India)and Dodhara Chandani (Nepal).
ii. Expeditiously complete work on final sections of the Jayanagar-Bardibas and Jogbani-Biratnagar railway lines.
iii. Welcoming the finalization of the Final Location Survey (FLS) of Raxaul-Kathmandu Rail Link, they agreed to collaborate on the development of the East-West Rail Link in Nepal to create an interoperable rail network between India and Nepal, prioritising the Bardibas–Nijgadh section and the Birgunj–Nijgadh link.
iv. Further enhance road connectivity between India and Nepal through new motorable bridges and trading points.
v. Augment cross-border petroleum supply infrastructure, including through construction of a new pipeline connecting Siliguri (India) and Jhapa (Nepal), and explore the possibility of a gas pipeline between India and Nepal.
vi. Building on the linkage of India's UPI with Nepal's national payment system, the two sides agreed to expedite implementation of cross-border retail payments.
vii. Cooperate in integrated infrastructure planning and connectivity, through platforms such as PM Gati Shakti, which Nepal may consider adapting to its own spatial and development priorities.
viii. Keep the international border between India and Nepal open, secure and well-regulated, and to strengthen cooperation against cross-border crime and illegal activities.
III. Energy, Water Resources and Climate Resilience:
Recognizing the immense potential for India and Nepal to deepen cooperation in the areas of energy, water resources and climate resilience, both sides agreed to strengthen institutional cooperation, promote mutually beneficial partnerships, and advance collaborative efforts towards sustainable, resilient and inclusive development. Towards this end:
i. In keeping with the India-Nepal Joint Vision Document for Power Sector Cooperation, India will encourage more investments in Nepal’s hydropower and transmission infrastructure while Nepal will provide appropriate cooperation and facilitation, including an enabling and mutually-beneficial framework for such investments. The authorities concerned will explore the possibility of further enhancing power trade, based on mutual benefit and market demand, with a view to expanding power trade between India and Nepal.
ii. Both sides will accelerate work on the implementation of on-going and envisaged hydropower and multipurpose projects, including the Pancheshwar and Saptakoshi & Sunkoshi multipurpose projects, to harness water resources for mutual benefit and to mitigate the adverse impacts arising due to floods.
iii. The two sides agreed to a proactive partnership on disaster risk reduction, early warning and post-disaster recovery to protect lives, livelihoods and infrastructure.
iv. They agreed to institutionalize real-time, two-way sharing of hydro-meteorological data, glacial lake monitoring, and early warning. They agreed to enhance cooperation between relevant agencies of both countries in the form of joint HADR exercises, capacity building, training and humanitarian support.
v. They agreed to enhance cooperation within multilateral organisations including the International Solar Alliance, the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, ICIMOD and the International Big Cat Alliance.
vi. Both sides agreed to collaborate in the development of additional energy sources from solar to sub-surface, including through a pilot project on green hydrogen in Nepal.
vii. India will facilitate the training of Nepali youth professionals, officials and experts in areas related to environment such as policy-making, regulation, standards, forestry, risk mapping, and climate resilient agriculture.
viii. India will also share expertise in rejuvenating water bodies and combating groundwater contamination.
IV. Good Governance:
There is considerable affinity between Nepal’s priorities related to good governance and the approach adopted by India, especially in matters related to the adoption of digital technology, and making the citizen-government interface more transparent, convenient and effective. Towards this end:
i. In accordance with globally recognized principles of digital sovereignty and data protection, to enable the implementation of the ‘Digital Nepal Framework’, technical expertise and best practices in digital public infrastructure in digital identity, payments and e-governance will be exchanged.
ii. Training of Nepali civil servants in India will be arranged through the National Centre for Good Governance.
iii. Both sides will share experiences and best practices among legislatures at national and provincial levels.
iv. They will strengthen cooperation in local governance through exchange of visits and training programmes at the relevant agencies of India.
V. Technology, Space and Innovation:
To encourage greater adoption and use of technology, and in accordance with Nepal’s objective of becoming a technology hub, and considering India’s strengths in these areas, the India-Nepal partnership will seek to deliver initiatives such as:
i. Expansion of the Indian-Nepal Startup Partnership Network (IN-SPAN), including through training and mentorship of Nepali startups in India, and setting up a Startup Centre of Excellence in Kathmandu and a Digital Nomads and Innovation Hub in Pokhara.
ii. Development of Digital Parks and data centres in Nepal, including through the facilitation of private investment.
iii. Enhancing bilateral cooperation in AI, including the development of a Large Language Model for the Nepali language, inter-alia, through collaboration with Bhashini.
iv. Strengthening cooperation in the domain of space including through collaboration between the Nepal Academy of Science and Technology and relevant Nepali agencies with ISRO and IN-SPACE for satellite development, earth observation, remote sensing for disaster management, and capacity building.
v. Enhancing cooperation in emerging telecommunication technologies such as 5G/6G and other next-generation networks.
VI. Education and Skill Development:
Recognizing the importance of skill development and capacity building, both countries will work to achieve stronger cooperation in training, human resource development, and academic exchanges, including through the following:
i. Opening of branches/campuses of reputed Indian higher educational institutions in Nepal will be explored, beginning with an IIT.
ii. Building on the highly successful ongoing scholarship schemes, scholarships and training opportunities in newer disciplines such as law, technology, and AI will be added for Nepali students.
iii. Exchanges of faculty and experts will be encouraged and institutionalized apart from stronger collaborations between academic and training institutions.
iv. A vocational training institute will be established through Indian assistance for imparting skills and training to the youth of Nepal in areas relevant for manufacturing, services and entrepreneurship.
VII. Sports:
To strengthen Nepal’s emphasis on the growth of sports and development of relevant infrastructure, India and Nepal will work together on the following main initiatives:
i. India will support the establishment of a national cricket coaching/training academy in Nepal apart from supporting the development of cricket infrastructure at the national and provincial levels.
ii. Players from provincial cricket teams of Nepal will be provided the opportunity to train in India at national training academies.
iii. Similar opportunities in other sports such as badminton, tennis, shooting, and athletics will also be explored, including for development of modern multi-sports centers in Nepal.
iv. Collaboration in mountain sports will be explored, including by undertaking joint expeditions.
v. Encouraging the concerned sporting bodies/authorities in both countries to explore opportunities for players from India and Nepal to participate in each other’s sporting leagues in games such as cricket, football and others.
VIII. Culture and Tourism:
Cultural linkages between both countries have been among the most important pillars of the bilateral relationship. To further enrich this vibrant interaction:
i. India and Nepal will partner to develop religious tourism circuits and new destinations. This will include development of Ramayana, Buddhist and Shiv–Shakti circuits by linking Janakpur–Ayodhya, Lumbini–Bodhgaya–Sarnath–Kushinagar and Kathmandu (Pashupatinath)–Varanasi, and through sister-city agreements.
ii. They agreed to hold an annual youth cultural festival alternately in Nepal and India, and to expand training and exchanges for artists in film-making, theatre and the fine arts.
iii. Collaboration between Nalanda University and Lumbini Buddhist University (LBU) will be strengthened through the establishment of a Nalanda Centre at LBU.
iv. They agreed to facilitate collaboration among young entrepreneurs in tourism and hospitality, and encourage familiarization visits of social media influencers and content creators to promote two-way tourism.
IX. Health:
Government of Nepal’s emphasis on an integrated model of basic healthcare across the country has considerable synergy with India’s approach towards health. In view of the existing complementarities and to nurture stronger cooperation in this domain, both sides will:
i. Strengthen healthcare infrastructure by continuing to undertake projects, under the High-Impact Community Development Project (HICDP) modality, for the construction of health posts, birthing centres, and hospitals as per the needs of Government of Nepal.
ii. Collaborate for upgrading the National Medical Laboratory of Nepal.
iii. Establish India–Nepal Jan Aushadhi Kendras to improve access to affordable quality medicines.
iv. Organize customized training programmes in health-related fields under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation Programme (ITEC) for capacity building of healthcare professionals of Nepal.
v. Foster linkages between premier medical institutions of both countries and encourage student and faculty exchanges.
vi. Strengthen research collaboration between Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and Nepal Health Research Council (NHRC), and the drug regulatory authorities of India (CDSCO) and Nepal (Department of Drug Administration).
X. Agriculture:
India and Nepal enjoy considerable interaction in this domain including experience sharing, training and the conclusion of framework documents. In order to further enhance forward looking engagement in this sector, the two sides will:
i. Establish an Agro-Industrial Park in Chitwan with India’s grant assistance to provide value addition to Nepali agricultural products.
ii. Expedite implementation of the Work Plan for 2026-2030 between Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and Nepal Agricultural Research Council (NARC).
iii. Organize customized training programmes in agriculture and livestock-related fields for capacity building of officials, farmers and other agriculture-related professionals of Nepal.
iv. Establish an ICAR Centre of Excellence in Nepal, link leading agricultural universities, and organise tailored training for Nepali officials, farmers and entrepreneurs in agriculture and livestock.
Implementation Modalities
The two Prime Ministers decided to activate the High-Level Monitoring Group, led by the Foreign Secretary of Nepal and the Ambassador of India. This Monitoring Group will meet at least once in six months and ensure expedited implementation of envisaged projects, ideas and initiatives, and facilitate relevant clearances/approvals.
Both leaders agreed that the High-Level Monitoring Group will submit its report to the India-Nepal Joint Commission, co-chaired by the Foreign Ministers of both countries. The leaders decided that the next meeting of the India-Nepal Joint Commission will be held in 2027.
The Prime Ministers expressed confidence that this Joint Vision document provides the blueprint for an aspirational, modern and mutually-beneficial partnership between two friendly countries, and directed officials from both India and Nepal to work towards the realisation of this shared vision.

title: English Translation of Prime Minister’s Press Statement during the Joint Press Statement with the Prime Minister of Nepal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 2:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Your Excellency, Prime Minister Balendra Shah ji,
Delegates from both countries,
Friends from the media
Namaskaar!
It is my great pleasure to extend a warm welcome to His Excellency Mr. Balendra Shah on his first bilateral visit to India since taking office as Prime Minister of Nepal.
A few months ago, when he addressed the United Nations as the world’s youngest Prime Minister, we had a clear glimpse of his vision and foresight. And today, during our discussions over the past few hours, I have witnessed his clear vision and unwavering commitment to the future of Nepal and to India-Nepal relations.
The historic mandate entrusted to him by the people of Nepal this year reflects the aspirations and hopes of the country's younger generation.
India has always been a committed partner in Nepal's journey towards becoming a strong and prosperous nation. Guided by this spirit, we have taken several important decisions today to elevate our bilateral relations to new heights.
Friends,
The relationship between India and Nepal is not merely one of neighbourhood, it is rooted in a deep sense of kinship and enduring trust. Our joys are shared, as are our challenges. We are partners in each other's progress and a source of support for one another in times of difficulty.
We express our deepest condolences over the loss of lives caused by the devastating floods that struck Nepal in August. Today, we also announce a Development Cooperation Package worth NPR 24,000 crore to support Nepal's reconstruction and long-term development.
Our resolve will be to ensure that the lives of affected families return to normal, new opportunities are created, and Nepal's capacity to effectively address future disasters is further strengthened.
Friends,
The relationship between India and Nepal is woven together by the threads of shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. Lord Ram and Mata Sita are enduring symbols of our shared civilisation and faith.
In 2018, on the sacred land of Janakpur, I had said, “Without Nepal, our pilgrimages are incomplete; without Nepal, even our Lord Ram is incomplete.”
In 2024, the Pran Pratishtha ceremony of Ram Lalla was held in Ayodhya. This historic occasion infused our shared faith with renewed vigour. Since then, millions of devotees have been visiting Ayodhya to seek the blessings of Ram Lalla. In 2025 alone, nearly 300 million devotees from across India and the world visited Ayodhya.
With the launch of the 'Sarayu-Kamala Express' train service today, we are adding a new dimension to this sacred bond. It will make it easier for devotees visiting Ayodhya to also travel to Janakpur and seek the blessings of Mata Sita.
We will also work together to enhance connectivity between sacred Buddhist sites in both countries, including Lumbini and Bodh Gaya, as well as other sites associated with Shiva Shakti and Buddha.
Friends,
Today, we have inaugurated the Dharchula road bridge between Uttarakhand and Nepal and laid the foundation stone for the Integrated Check Post at Banbasa. We will also expedite the development of the Dodhara-Chandani Integrated Check Post on the Nepalese side. These initiatives will facilitate trade and the movement of people between Uttarakhand and Nepal.
At the same time, we will accelerate road, rail and border connectivity projects between Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, other Indian states and Nepal. To further facilitate Nepal's transit trade, we will provide access to the ports of Kandla and Paradip. I am confident that all these efforts towards better trade, connectivity and investment will give fresh impetus to Nepal's economic development.
Friends,
Nepal's rivers hold immense potential for clean energy generation. India's vast energy market can transform this potential into a strong foundation for Nepal's economic prosperity.
The laying of the foundation stone for the Lower Arun Hydroelectric Project today, along with our commitment to the timely completion of Arun-3, is an integral part of this vision.
Friends,
For several years, India has been a reliable supplier of petroleum products and other essential commodities to Nepal. In keeping with the spirit of our Neighbourhood First Policy, despite the serious challenges related to oil supplies this year, we have ensured the continued supply of fuel, fertilisers and other essential commodities to Nepal.
The inauguration of Phase Two of the Motihari-Amlekhgunj Pipeline and the laying of the foundation stone for the Jhapa Petroleum Terminal today will further strengthen this partnership.
Friends,
Nepal's younger generation is brimming with talent, energy and great aspirations. India wishes to be a committed partner in helping them realise their dreams.
To translate this commitment into action, we will establish a Start-up Incubator, an Innovation Hub, and an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal.
We will expand scholarship opportunities for Nepali students in India in the fields of Law and Technology. We will also cooperate in the development of an Agro-Industrial Park in Nepal to promote food processing and value addition.
Friends,
The story of the Ramayana is reaching the younger generation and audiences across the world through films and modern technology. We want young creators from India and Nepal to work together to take our shared heritage to the world through new and innovative mediums. In this direction, we will welcome a large delegation from Nepal at the next WAVES Summit.
We will also step up our cooperation in the development of sports infrastructure and the training of players in Nepal, particularly in cricket.
Your Excellency,
Today, we are unveiling a Joint Vision Document to chart a new course for our shared future. It serves as a blueprint for the collective realisation of our respective aspirations of a “Viksit Bharat and Samunnat Nepal”.
We have clear objectives, mutual trust, and the capability to realise them. Above all, we have the blessings of Mata Sita, Lord Ram and Lord Buddha with us.
I am confident that, guided by this same spirit, we will translate our shared vision into tangible achievements and together write a new golden chapter in India-Nepal relations.
Long live India–Nepal friendship!
Thank you very much.

title: Ayush Pavilion Emerges as a Major Attraction at India International Trade Fair 2026
subtitle: Draws Large Crowds with Free Healthcare Consultations, Yoga Sessions and Interactive Wellness Activities
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 12:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Ayush is showcasing India’s diverse traditional healthcare systems at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, being held from 13 to 27 November at Hall No. 2, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Ayush Pavilion is offering visitors an engaging experience through healthcare consultations, interactive activities, traditional dietary preparations, medicinal plant displays and educational presentations highlighting the relevance of Ayush systems in promoting preventive healthcare and healthy living.This year’s Ayush Pavilion at IITF is themed "Ayush Ki Virasat Se Swasth Bharat Ka Vikaas" (आयुष की विरासत से स्वस्थ भारत का विकास), in alignment with the overarching theme of IITF,  "Development and Heritage" (विकास और विरासत).
The pavilion brings together institutions and research councils under the Ministry of Ayush, presenting a wide range of activities that connect traditional knowledge with everyday health practices. The CCRAS–CARI is providing Ayurveda OPD services and Prakriti Pariksha, along with information on preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and Ayurvedic wellness. The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, is presenting commonly used herbs and spices, including Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Arjuna, Amla, Haridra and Guduchi, with information on their classical applications and relevance to health promotion. Visitors are also being sensitised to the importance of appropriate dosage, individual health conditions and professional guidance before using medicinal herbs.
The National Institute of Ayurveda (NIA), Jaipur, is showcasing Ayush Aahar products such as Ragi Cookies, Triphala Jam, Aloe Vera Gel and herbal Lip Balm. Interactive attractions include Ayurvedic Snakes and Ladders based on Ahara (diet) and Vihara (lifestyle), along with virtual reality experiences offering visualisation of human body systems. IEC materials are also being displayed to create awareness about Prakruti, Panchakarma, Ayurvedic cooking and the role of Ayurveda in daily life.
Rashtriya Ayurveda Vidyapeeth (RAV) is promoting Ayurveda-based food innovations through the display of POSHAK cookies, Ayurvedic bread and the traditional drink Pankam. Activities such as “Dadi Se Puchho” and “Millets on the Wheel” are engaging visitors while spreading awareness about traditional dietary practices, the nutritional benefits of millets and healthy living.
The Morarji Desai National Institute of Yoga (MDNIY) is conducting regular yoga demonstrations and sessions on a dedicated platform at the pavilion. Visitors are also receiving personalised yoga consultations based on their age, health concerns and lifestyle. Yoga quizzes and asana competitions are further encouraging participation, with visitors showing interest in incorporating yoga into their daily routines.
The Unani stall, managed by the Regional Research Institute of Unani Medicine (RRIUM), New Delhi, under the Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine (CCRUM), is highlighting traditional Unani dietary preparations and healthcare practices. Visitors are being offered tastings of Unani Qahwa, Hareera, Halwa Gheekawar, Gulkand and Murabba Amla. A modified digital Mizaj Assessment Kiosk is enabling visitors to assess their temperament and receive personalised dietary advice. The stall also features digital presentations and documentaries on Unani medicine. On 18 and 19 November, the Unani OPD provided free consultations and medicines to 151 patients.
The Siddha stall, managed by the Central Council for Research in Siddha (CCRS) and the National Institute of Siddha (NIS), Chennai, raises awareness of Siddha principles, preventive healthcare practices, and therapeutic applications. The display covers Siddha Ahar, nutrition, lifestyle modification, diagnostic methods, traditional formulations and therapies, including Varma therapy. Digital presentations, documentaries and IEC materials are being used to engage visitors. The stall also highlights NIS's academic and research activities, including its BSMS, MD (Siddha), and PhD programmes, encouraging students to explore education and careers in Siddha.
The Central Council for Research in Yoga & Naturopathy (CCRYN) is presenting Yoga and Naturopathy through digital audio-visual content, IEC material and an Ayush Aahar display. Visitors are being introduced to healthy snack options such as Makhana Ladoo, Peanut Ladoo, Til Ladoo and Namkeen. Free consultations on Yoga, Naturopathy, dietary practices and lifestyle modifications were also provided on 17 and 18 November.
The National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa is offering visitors insights into the ancient healing traditions of the Himalayan region. The stall features detailed information on Sowa-Rigpa diet, therapeutic regimens and herbal formulations, with practitioners offering personalised guidance based on classical Sowa-Rigpa texts.
The National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB) is highlighting the importance of medicinal plants through live displays, information material and the distribution of Satavari medicinal plants. Plants featuring QR codes are helping visitors access information, while brochures, pamphlets and the comic book “Professor Ayushman” are being distributed to promote awareness about medicinal plants and their uses.
Through its diverse displays and interactive activities, the Ayush Pavilion at IITF 2026 is providing a platform for visitors to experience India’s traditional healthcare systems and learn about their role in preventive healthcare, nutrition and wellness. The pavilion reflects the Ministry of Ayush’s continued efforts to promote public awareness and bring Ayush practices closer to people through accessible, engaging and educational initiatives.

“Lakhpati Didis, permanent houses, rural roads, Viksit Bharat - G RAM G and watershed development have transformed the lives of the rural poor”: Shri Shivraj Singh

ICAR innovations have increased farmers’ incomes, delivering an economic return of ₹13.85 for every rupee invested

“Celebrate this achievement with joy and a sense of occasion”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan appreciates the efforts of everyone, from Section Officers to Secretaries

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan sits among employees for direct interaction and seeks their suggestions; the next goal is to make a mark in global markets through FTAs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 9:11PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India has achieved unprecedented, extraordinary and historic milestones in the field of poverty eradication. According to the World Bank’s recent report, nearly 500 million people in the country have moved out of poverty, while the rate of extreme poverty has declined from 27.1 per cent to just 2.6 per cent. This remarkable progress reflects the contribution of several sectors and government initiatives, particularly agriculture and allied activities, agricultural research, land resources and rural development. To assess the role played by these areas in the achievement and discuss the strategy for the road ahead, a special one-day workshop was organised today at the Dr Ambedkar International Centre in New Delhi. The joint workshop was chaired by Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Union Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare Shri Bhagirath Choudhary and Union Minister of State for Rural Development Shri Kamlesh Paswan also participated. Describing the country’s progress, Shri Chouhan called it an “extraordinary, unimaginable and unprecedented miracle”.
The workshop brought together the senior-most officials of all four departments whose work and initiatives were being reviewed. Those present included Secretary, Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, Shri Atish Chandra; Secretary, Department of Rural Development, Shri Rohit Kansal; Secretary, Department of Land Resources, Shri Dilip Kumar; and Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Dr M. L. Jat. Senior officials and scientists from the four departments also attended, along with Section Officers, Assistant Section Officers and a large number of other officers and employees. The participation of staff across different levels reflected the workshop’s focus not only on reviewing departmental achievements, but also on recognising the contribution of those involved in taking policies and schemes from the planning stage to implementation.
Lifting 500 million people out of poverty, more than the population of the United States, is a miracle
Addressing officers and employees of the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, ICAR, Department of Rural Development and Department of Land Resources, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that the achievement India had secured under the leadership and guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi was truly extraordinary, remarkable and unimaginable. The World Bank itself had acknowledged that no other country in the world had reduced poverty at such a rapid pace. The fact that nearly 500 million people had moved above the poverty line represented a historic development, particularly given the scale of the population involved. Shri Chouhan said that this progress was the result of the Prime Minister’s leadership, vision and hard work, but it was also important to recognise the contribution made by every officer and employee in the two ministries. The achievement, he stressed, was not the work of any one individual or department; it reflected the collective effort of people working across the government machinery to deliver development and improve lives.
“You have not merely framed schemes; you have built the nation”: Celebrate this achievement
Encouraging officers and employees, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that this success had not come about on its own. Behind it lay the hard work, dedication and sustained efforts of everyone who had contributed to the implementation of government programmes. He urged those attending the workshop to participate with a sense of joy and celebration, observing that when the country had achieved something so significant, the happiness and pride it inspired should also be visible on their faces. Shri Chouhan recalled that the Prime Minister had emphasised that “you have not merely framed schemes; you have built the nation”. He explained that review meetings are generally attended by senior officials, but he had consciously decided to make this workshop different. He wanted colleagues at every level, from Section Officers and Assistant Section Officers to Secretaries, to be present because they were the foundation stones of the administrative system and the work on files began at these levels. He told the employees that they were not merely witnesses to the country’s development journey, but its true drivers and participants. Demonstrating his intention to engage directly with them, Shri Chouhan left the stage and sat among the audience, speaking with employees and seeking to understand their experiences on the ground and their suggestions.
Resolve to bring those still left behind out of poverty
Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan said that people work not merely to earn a livelihood, but also to find purpose in their lives and serve the people of the country. He observed that every stage in the journey of a government scheme involves the contribution of employees. Whether a scheme is developed from the grassroots, considered and approved by the Cabinet, or eventually implemented on the ground, the efforts of people working at different levels are essential to its success. He said that two major commitments made by the Prime Minister now lay before the nation. The first was to ensure that those who had already risen above the poverty line did not fall back below it under any circumstances. The second was to rapidly bring the remaining 2.6 to 2.7 per cent of the population out of poverty and improve their standard of living. Shri Chouhan emphasised that the progress achieved so far must be protected, while the government continued working to reach those who had yet to benefit sufficiently from the country’s development. The task ahead, therefore, was both to sustain the gains made and to ensure that the remaining people were also able to lead better lives.
Agriculture growth rate reaches a historic 4.45%; ICAR research delivers returns of 13.85 times the investment
Highlighting the achievements of the agriculture sector, Union Minister Shri Chouhan said that the past 12 years had witnessed remarkable progress, with work being undertaken in agriculture that the country could take pride in. He pointed out that even during the Green Revolution, the agriculture growth rate generally remained in the range of 3 to 3.5 per cent. India’s decadal agriculture growth rate had now reached the historic level of 4.45 per cent, surpassing the levels recorded during that period. Among the key initiatives contributing to the sector’s progress, he highlighted the direct assistance of more than ₹4.66 lakh crore provided through the PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi under the Department of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The sector had also recorded foodgrain production of 376.56 million tonnes and horticulture production of 386.91 million tonnes. Affordable agricultural credit, crop insurance, natural farming, the establishment of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and digital initiatives such as AgriStack had further supported farmers and contributed to increasing their incomes. Together, these measures reflected the progress made in strengthening agricultural production and improving the support available to farmers.
A presentation by the Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE/ICAR) highlighted the economic returns generated by scientific research and innovation. It stated that every rupee invested in agricultural research and education had yielded an economic benefit of ₹13.85, while investment in animal husbandry research had generated a return of ₹20.81. Since 2014, a total of 3,436 new crop varieties had been released, of which 93 per cent were climate-resilient. The presentation also highlighted the contribution of biofortified crop varieties, fish production of 19.78 million tonnes and the availability of more than 500 agricultural machines. In addition, digital outreach through Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) was reaching five crore farmers every year. These research-led developments, technological interventions and knowledge-sharing efforts had helped strengthen the rural economy and extend the benefits of agricultural science to farmers across the country.
Rural development and DoLR schemes have transformed the lives of villages and the rural poor
The workshop also examined in detail the impact of schemes implemented by the Department of Rural Development and the Department of Land Resources. Shri Chouhan said that these departments had played a highly significant role in the country's progress towards poverty eradication. Presentations highlighted the reach of several rural development initiatives. Under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission, more than 10 crore women had been connected with self-help groups, and 3.76 crore women had so far become ‘Lakhpati Didis’. The Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) had enabled the construction of 3.99 crore permanent houses, while the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) had created a network of 7.99 lakh kilometres of all-weather rural roads. Under Viksit Bharat - G RAM G (VB-G RAM G), rural households are now assured of 125 days of employment. Social assistance programmes and 99.9 per cent transparency in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) have also helped empower the last person in the queue. These initiatives have contributed to changing the lives of rural families by supporting livelihoods, providing housing, improving connectivity and strengthening the delivery of assistance to beneficiaries.
Under the Department of Land Resources (DoLR), the watershed development component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (WDC-PMKSY) has supported water conservation and land improvement works across 3.40 crore hectares. These interventions have directly benefited 61.15 lakh farmers. The work has contributed to an increase in irrigated areas and milk production, while farmers’ average annual incomes have recorded growth of up to 70 per cent. The figures presented at the workshop highlighted the contribution of watershed development to improving land and water resources, strengthening agricultural activity and supporting the livelihoods of farming communities. The programme's impact was also reflected in the number of farmers who had directly benefited from these interventions and the reported improvement in their annual incomes.
Suggestions sought to improve budgets and schemes; call to take achievements to the public
During the concluding session of the workshop, Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan extended an open invitation to officers and employees to share their ideas and suggestions. He emphasised that the achievements made so far did not mean there was no scope for further improvement. Several useful suggestions had already been received on schemes such as PM-KISAN and e-NAM. He encouraged everyone to write to him without hesitation if they had any ideas concerning the budget, changes to existing schemes or the introduction of new initiatives that could help increase farmers’ incomes. Shri Chouhan said that he would also hold informal, department-wise meetings with employees working at lower levels in the future. As the head of the department, he assured colleagues that he would remain accessible and approachable to everyone, regardless of their position or level of responsibility. He invited them to contribute their practical experience and ideas to the process of improving government programmes and making them more effective.
Shri Chouhan also placed particular emphasis on the need to ensure that the departments’ achievements and public welfare initiatives did not remain confined to files and formal communications, but were effectively taken to the people and farmers. He said that communicating the work being done by the departments and its impact on people's lives was an important responsibility. Giving an example, he observed that when officials go directly to the ground and engage with people, the positive message reaches the entire country. He stressed that the development journey was far from over and that the targets set for 2029, 2030–31 and ‘Viksit Bharat @2047’ had to be achieved on time. Referring to the Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), he said that the next objective was to enable Indian agricultural products to make their mark in markets across the world. The country now had to build on the progress achieved in agriculture and ensure that its products reached and competed successfully in global markets.

title: Ministry of Coal amends Mineral Concession Rules, 1960 and extends accreditation period of Accredited Prospecting Agencies and Mining Plan Preparing Agencies from three to five years
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Coal has notified the Mineral Concession (Third Amendment) Rules, 2026 vide G.S.R. 999(E) dated 17 November 2026. Subsequently, the accreditation cycle has been extended from three to five years for Accredited Prospecting Agencies (APA) and Mining Plan Preparing Agencies (MPPA).
The reform will reduce the number of periodic assessments and re-accreditations, thereby saving the time of accredited agencies on repetitive assessment and accreditation. The longer validity of accreditation will ensure continuity in the preparation of geological reports and mining plans, which are prerequisites for operationalization of coal and lignite blocks.
This reform is a significant step towards Ease of Doing Business and trust-based governance in the coal sector.

title: Ministry of Coal issues Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Coal has issued the “Guidelines for preparation of Mining Plan and Mine Closure Plan for Coal and Lignite Mines, 2026” on 20 November 2026. The Guidelines shall come into force 30 days from the date of its issue. The Guidelines provide an outcome-oriented framework for systematic and scientific mine planning and mine closure. It complements the existing statutory framework and avoids redundancy in compliance requirements covered under other statutory provisions.
Under the Guidelines, defined timelines have been laid down at different stages of scrutiny and approval, ensuring a time-bound decision-making process. The timeline for reimbursement from the escrow account for mine closure works has been reduced to one month from the receipt of claim, with provision for test-check of claims. In addition, the ambit of agencies for verification of five-yearly claims for withdrawal from the escrow account has been widened.
Keeping pace with emerging technologies, the Guidelines recognize Underground Coal Gasification as a mining method, and the “Guidelines for preparation and approval of Mining Plan for Coal and Lignite Blocks/Mines for Underground Gasification 2026” have been made an integral part of these Guidelines. Project proponents have also been given greater flexibility in line with prevailing conditions, enabling faster operationalization of mines.
The Guidelines are expected to improve Ease of Doing Business through simpler, practical and time-bound processes, and to accelerate the operationalization of mines, supporting the country’s energy security. It provides a clear and focused regulatory framework, while promoting scientific mine closure and repurposing for the benefit of local communities.

title: Gyan Bharatam Session at the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum Reconnects the Manuscript Heritage; Language, Script and Manuscript Traditions
subtitle: Scholars and delegates from SCO Member States and Dialogue Partners discuss manuscript preservation, translation, digitisation and international cooperation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                23 NOV 2026 1:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India’s manuscript heritage, encompassing knowledge of polity, economy, medicine, mathematics, astronomy, agriculture and sustainable living, reflects a rich civilizational journey in which knowledge travelled across regions through lipi (script), bhāṣā (language) and jñāna (knowledge). Rooted in the spirit of the Ṛgvedic prayer “ā no bhadrāḥ kratavo yantu viśvataḥ” (let noble thoughts come to us from all sides), this shared legacy was the focus of Session IV on “Language, Literature, Script and Manuscript Traditions”, convened by the Ministry of Culture under the Gyan Bharatam Mission on 22 November 2026 at Purana Qila (Old Fort), New Delhi. The session brought together eminent scholars, experts and delegates from SCO Member States and Dialogue Partners to deliberate on the shared manuscript heritage and avenues for collaboration.
The session was part of the 1st SCO Civilization Dialogue Forum, held from 20 to 22 November 2026 and inaugurated by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India Shri Narendra Modi.
Shri Inderjeet Singh, CEO (Gyan Bharatam) & Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture,
briefed participants from SCO countries on the Gyan Bharatam Mission and its operational activities to the participation SCO Countries: Survey and Cataloguing; Conservation and Capacity Building; Technology and Digitization; Linguistics and Translation; and Research, Publication and Outreach. He highlighted the key features of AI and its integrated features, Gyan-MitramAI, Pandulipi Darpana and BharatiyaGPT, and the milestone achieved that over 1.26 crore manuscripts have been reported through the National Manuscript Survey.
Emphasising the collaborative vision of the Mission, he stated, “For the Gyan Bharatam Mission, this is both a responsibility and an invitation to work together.” He also highlighted the significance of Indic scripts across the SCO region and the role of manuscripts in fostering global dialogue and building a global digital repository of knowledge.
Prof. Anirban Dash, Project Director, Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture
,
moderated the session and welcomed the participants. He observed that language gives voice to our thoughts, Language and literature preserve them, and these manuscripts carry wisdoms across time and places. He highlighted how knowledge travelled across mountains and seas, underwent translation and adaptation, and became part of the intellectual life of diverse societies.
Thereafter, the session begin with discussion over 4 key themes, “Many tongues, Many scripts: India’s Linguistic and Script Heritage and its imprint on Asian Languages; Literature in Motion: transmission, translation, and Localization of Indian texts across Asia; Manuscripts Beyond Borders: The Global Presence and Dispersal of India’s Manuscript Heritage; Reconnecting Dispersed Knowledge: Gyan Bharatam and the Digital Future of Manuscript Heritage”.
Prof. Rajnish Kumar Mishra, Professor, SSIS, Jawaharlal Nehru University, emphasized India's vivid linguistic and script heritage and its imprint on Asian languages. He spoke on the varied nature, concepts and modes of expression that spread across the world through the communication and writings of our great seers, and noted that Indian culture also spread across the oceans via the Silk Route. He talked about scholars such as Shankaracarya, Ramashekhar, Acarya Abhinavagupta and others, and also threw light on the different regional manuscript traditions and recessions.
Prof. K.K. Mishra, Head and Associate Professor, Department of Sanskrit, University of Calcutta, focused on enhancing the pathway for digitisation, translation into more languages, multiple uses of AI, and global accessibility via the establishment of NDR. He referred to the BnF, Thailand and Vietnam, Mongolia and Russia, Google Arts & Culture, and bilateral and archival ties, and also touched upon translators, pilgrims and Nalanda.
Dr. Viswajanani J. Sattigeri, Head, TKDL Unit, spoke on Gyan Bharatam and the digital future of manuscript heritage. She stressed the need to protect our knowledge from piracy and spoke on the published nature of our traditional knowledge, IPR, patent codes, codified metadata on the database, and controlled access to avoid duplication and misappropriation, like TKDL.
Prof. K. Rama Subramaniyam, IIT Bombay,
spoke on manuscripts and their importance in interpreting things rightly, as it shapes thought, expression and mind. Citing the example of the Pañcatantra, which has been translated into over 50 foreign languages, such as Arabic, Persian and others, he stressed the need to keep translations of the content free from biased interpretation. He observed that knowledge is bound to decay and has to be preserved. A manuscript preserved for hundreds of years is treasured not only for its content but also for the journey of time and traditions it carries.
Delegates from several SCO countries, including Iran, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Cambodia, Uzbekistan, Laos and Nepal, actively participated in the discussions. They shared their respective efforts and initiatives for manuscript preservation and expressed interest in collaborating with Gyan Bharatam, Ministry of Culture, Government of India, in various manuscript related activities.
The session concluded with a shared commitment to strengthen cooperation in manuscript preservation, script training, comparative literary studies, research and translation, cataloguing, academic exchanges, authorised digital access and joint research, reaffirming the role of shared heritage and knowledge traditions in fostering cultural understanding and cooperation across the SCO region.
